transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because of what's been happening at my job. I'm a waitress, and... what really scared everyone at work is that I started just freezing up in the middle of a busy service. 

Or I'll start doing things completely out of order. Like, the other day I just ended up standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. I don't really know why I was doing it, but it freaked my coworkers out, so... that's why I'm here.
When you 'freeze up' or act this way, do you have any memory of what happened during those moments, or is there a gap in your memory afterward?

No, I remember it. It's not like I black out or anything. I know I'm standing there, and I can hear myself saying the numbers. I just... I can't really seem to snap out of it or move on to the next task. So, yeah, there's no gap in my memory. I just kind of get stuck.
Before these episodes start, do you notice any strange physical sensations, like an unusual smell, a rising feeling in your stomach, or a sudden sense of déjà vu?
No, I don't think so. I haven't smelled anything weird or felt anything like that in my stomach. And it's definitely not déjà vu. It just kind of happens, without any warning signs like that.
Outside of these specific episodes at work, do you find yourself feeling constantly worried or anxious about various aspects of your life, like your health, finances, or other daily responsibilities?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, like paying rent, but it's not constant. I'm not up at night stressing about my health or anything like that. It's just the stuff at work that's really bothering me right now.
During these episodes, do you notice any repetitive physical movements, such as picking at your clothes, smacking your lips, or twitching in any part of your body?

No, I don't think I do any of that. I'm not... I don't pick at my clothes or smack my lips or anything. I really just stand there still while I'm stuck on the numbers. So, no, no twitching or weird movements like that.
During these moments when you feel 'stuck,' do you feel as though you are disconnected from your own body or as if you are watching yourself from the outside?

No, I don't feel like that. I'm definitely in my own body. I'm just... frozen, I guess. But I'm not watching myself from the outside or feeling disconnected or anything. I'm right there, just stuck on the numbers.
When you are in one of these 'stuck' states, can you respond if someone talks to you or asks you a question, or are you unable to communicate until the episode passes?

No, I can't really talk to anyone when it happens. That's what actually scared everyone at work. I would just freeze up right in the middle of a dinner service. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order... like, I'd just be standing over by the soda station, holding the key to the cash drawer, and I'd just keep repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out my checks. If someone tried to ask me a question, I couldn't really answer them until it was over.
During these moments when you are unable to respond to others, do you feel like you are in a dream-like state or that your consciousness is clouded in any way?

No, I wouldn't say it feels like a dream. It's not... cloudy or anything like that. My head is actually really clear, but it's just completely filled up with the numbers. I'm awake and I know where I am, I just can't snap out of it.
When you are stuck in these episodes, have your coworkers mentioned if your eyes look strange, such as fluttering, staring blankly without blinking, or if your face seems to change color?

No, nobody has ever said anything like that to me. They just said I was standing there repeating the numbers. They haven't mentioned my eyes doing anything weird or my face changing color. Just that I wouldn't answer them and I was stuck.
Are you aware of any specific emotional triggers, such as feeling overwhelmed, stressed, or angry, that occur immediately before these episodes start?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, work can be stressful sometimes, especially when it gets busy, but... I don't think I feel particularly angry or overwhelmed right before it happens. It just kind of starts on its own.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological condition, such as epilepsy, or have you ever had a significant head injury?

No, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with epilepsy or... any kind of neurological thing. And I haven't had any bad head injuries either, like a concussion or being in a bad accident. So, no, nothing like that.
During these episodes, or at any other time, do you ever feel like a different part of your personality or a different 'version' of yourself takes over and acts or speaks for you?

No, I don't feel like that at all. It's always just me. I don't feel like a different person or some other version of myself is taking over. I'm just... stuck in my own head, repeating those numbers. But it's definitely still me the whole time.
After the episode finally passes and you are able to move or speak again, do you feel confused, exhausted, or like you need to sleep?

No, I don't think so. Once it finally stops and I can move again, I just feel... normal, I guess. I'm not confused about what happened or where I am, and I don't feel completely exhausted or like I need to go to sleep right away. I just kind of pick up right where I left off.
During these episodes, do you ever find that you have moved or traveled to a place that you didn't intend to be, or that you have 'come to' in a different location than where you started?
No, that doesn't happen. I stay right where I am. I don't ever... wake up somewhere else or find myself in a place I didn't mean to go. I'm always exactly where I was when it started.
When you are repeating those table numbers, is it always the exact same sequence of numbers, or does the content change each time?

I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed if it's the exact same order every single time. It's always just the table numbers from work, but... I don't know if the actual sequence changes or not. I don't really keep track of the specific order, I'm just focused on repeating them.

When you are repeating these numbers, do you feel an internal pressure or an overwhelming urge to say them that only goes away once you've done it, or does it feel like you are physically unable to stop yourself regardless of what you want to do?

I don't think it's either of those. Um... I don't feel a pressure building up that makes me do it, like I have to get it out of my system. And it doesn't feel like my mouth is just moving on its own against my will, either. I just... I just find myself saying them. There isn't really a big urge behind it, it just kind of happens.

When you are repeating these numbers, do you feel that you are choosing to say them, even if it feels like something you 'have' to do, or does it feel like your speech is happening automatically without your active participation?

I'm not exactly sure. It doesn't really feel like a choice I'm making... like, I don't sit there and decide to start saying them. But I don't know if I'd call it totally automatic, either. It's hard to explain. I just sort of realize that I'm already doing it. I don't really know if I'm actively participating or not, to be honest.

When you finally stop repeating the numbers and can speak to your coworkers again, do you have any sense of being slightly 'foggy' or disoriented for a few minutes before you feel completely back to your normal self?

No, I don't think so. Um, once I stop saying them, I just go right back to whatever I was doing. I don't feel foggy or confused or anything like that. I just... I stop, and then I can talk to my coworkers normally right away.
Do you find that these episodes occur more frequently when you are feeling particularly overwhelmed or pressured by your workload?

I haven't really noticed a connection like that. Um, it doesn't seem to matter how busy the restaurant is or if I'm feeling stressed out about my tables. It just happens when it happens, whether it's the middle of the dinner rush or if we're completely dead.
When you are repeating these numbers, do you find the experience distressing or bothersome in the moment, or are you just calmly focused on the numbers?

It's... it's definitely bothersome, mostly because of how it affects everything else. Like, I'm focused on the numbers, but it's messing up my job. What really scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service. Or I'd do things totally out of order. Like, I'd just be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, just repeating those table numbers over and over, instead of actually closing out my checks. So yeah, it's distressing because I know I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
